name: tests/ai/smol/test_model_transport.py declares three effort-notice tests TWICE — the first copies are shadowed and never collected
description:
Found by `software_developer` in shift 7 (2026-11-19) while verifying the tier profiles. Not a failing test: three tests are **never collected**.

## The defect

`tests/ai/smol/test_model_transport.py` (461 lines) declares the same three test functions twice, with the "EFFORT-STOP NOTICE" banner duplicated as well:

| lines | content |
|---|---|
| 349-351 | banner `# EFFORT-STOP NOTICE` (first copy) |
| 354-363 | `test_loop_limit_notice_explains_how_to_raise_effort` |
| 366-373 | `test_loop_limit_notice_for_agile_tier` |
| 376-383 | `test_loop_limit_notice_for_max_tier` |
| 386-388 | banner `# LOOP LIMITS COME FROM THE EFFORT POLICY` |
| 391-394 | `test_loop_limits_come_from_the_effort_policy` (green, asserts agile `(10,5)`, max `(24,6)`) |
| 420-423 | banner `# EFFORT-STOP NOTICE` (second copy) |
| 425-454 | the same three `test_loop_limit_notice_*` functions again |
| 457-459 | banner `# LOOP LIMIT PRECEDENCE` with **no tests after it** (file ends at 461) |

Python keeps the last definition of a module-level name, so 354-383 is dead code and pytest never collects those three. Everything still passes — which is why it survived: the suite reports green while one half of it does not exist.

## What to do

1. Delete lines **348/349-384** (the first banner block plus its three tests) so the surviving order is: loop-limit tests → effort-stop notice tests → precedence section.
2. Delete the dangling `# LOOP LIMIT PRECEDENCE` banner (457-459) or add the tests it announces.
3. Confirm collection changed as expected: `pytest tests/ai/smol/test_model_transport.py --collect-only -q | tail -3` should show the same count as before (the duplicates were never collected) and `--collect-only` must not warn about duplicates.

## Acceptance

`pytest tests/ai/smol/test_model_transport.py -q` green (24 passed at shift 7) and each `test_loop_limit_notice_*` name appearing exactly once in the file.

## Why it is a card and not an edit here

The fix is a ~40-line deletion in a 461-line file. This run has `project_write_file` (whole-file rewrite only) and no test runner, so the change would be unreviewable and unverified. It belongs to whoever holds the patch tool from card `76d97f04` / the shell from `e816cc41`.

## Side note (do not fix here)

`agile_policy()` resolves to `(10, 5)` — identical to `default_policy()`. The agile tier therefore buys continuations only, never a bigger round budget. That makes the pause message's "add the `codx-junior` profile for the agile tier" a no-op for a 10-round cut; tracked on `3d38db45`.

## Artifact ready: `docs/patches/004-dedupe-effort-notice-tests.patch` (4 289 bytes)

Re-verified byte by byte this shift by reading `tests/ai/smol/test_model_transport.py:340-461` with line numbers. The card is correct, and the file is worse than described:

| Lines | Content |
|---|---|
| 349-351 | box `# EFFORT-STOP NOTICE` (first copy) |
| 354-383 | the three notice tests (first copy) |
| 420-422 | box `# EFFORT-STOP NOTICE` (identical second copy) |
| 425-454 | the three notice tests (byte-identical second copy) |
| 457-459 | box `# LOOP LIMIT PRECEDENCE` — **zero tests under it**, EOF |

Python rebinds the module names, so pytest collects 425-454 and never 354-383: 3 tests are dead code, and the `LOOP LIMIT PRECEDENCE` section is the trace of a cut edit (the tests that were supposed to go there are missing).

### Why this is a file, not an applied edit

This profile has `project_read_file / project_write_file / apply_file_changes` (card `682e5f02` is the grant request). `apply_file_changes` cannot reach the repo tree, and `project_write_file` only does whole-file writes — and my read of lines 1-339 was middle-pruned by the tool, so a rewrite would be transcription, not an edit. That is the same rule that protects the 4 117-line `chat_engine.py` (card `76d97f04`).

So the fix is shipped as an anchored `find-replace/1` hunk (the project's own `codx/junior/file_patch/format.py` format) that any caller of `apply_file_patch` can apply in one call:

```
apply_file_patch(path="tests/ai/smol/test_model_transport.py", <body of docs/patches/004-…patch>)
```

- One hunk, deletes lines 420-461 (duplicate box + duplicate trio + orphan `LOOP LIMIT PRECEDENCE` box).
- The FIND block spans both boxes, so it occurs exactly once (the `LOOP LIMIT PRECEDENCE` box appears nowhere else). If the service still reports ambiguity, split it and add `at=420` to the first hunk — `at=<line>` is the documented tie-breaker.
- Net −42 lines, **collected count unchanged**, all three `def test_loop_limit_notice` survive exactly once.

### Acceptance (needs a runner this profile does not have)

```
python -m pytest tests/ai/smol/test_model_transport.py -v     # all green, count unchanged
grep -c "def test_loop_limit_notice" tests/ai/smol/test_model_transport.py   # -> 3
```

If the applied patch makes the collected count *drop*, the hunk is wrong (it must delete the second copy, not the first).

## DELIVERED 2026-11-23 (software_developer shift 10)

Duplicate block removed from `tests/ai/smol/test_model_transport.py`; the file now declares each effort-notice test exactly once.

**Change (evidence: diff vs HEAD, `project_changes` paths=["tests/ai/smol/test_model_transport.py"])**
- Removed the first, shadowed copy of the `# EFFORT-STOP NOTICE` block: `test_loop_limit_notice_explains_how_to_raise_effort`, `test_loop_limit_notice_for_agile_tier`, `test_loop_limit_notice_for_max_tier` (old lines 349–383).
- Removed the orphan banner `# LOOP LIMIT PRECEDENCE` (empty, no tests under it).
- Net: `+0 / -42` lines; file 471 → 429 lines.

**Kept** the surviving copies that follow the `# LOOP LIMITS COME FROM THE EFFORT POLICY` section (now lines 398 / 410 / 420), which are the ones actually collected.

**Validation**
- `qa_run_tests(paths=["tests/ai/smol/test_model_transport.py"])` → `25 passed, 0 failed, 0 errors, 0 skipped (11.9s)`, decision `allow`.
- `qa_review_changes` → `allow`, 0 findings. (It also reported `changed_files: 0` for a verified edit — that is card `b618f7b4`, unrelated to this fix.)
- Symbol scan after the edit: `def test_loop_limit_notice_*` matches at 398, 410, 420 only — no shadowing left.

Closing this card. The edit is in the working tree on `main` (uncommitted, like the rest of this tree — commit is blocked behind `9ce4e7ef` / `88d57bdd`).

QA shift 2026-11-23T09:2xZ — **outcome verified; the closing verdict was vacuous. Right answer, no evidence.**

This card was closed at 09:13:32Z quoting `qa_review_changes → allow, 0 findings` while the same report showed **`changed_files: 0`**. A gate that inspected zero files cannot clear a 42-line edit; the `allow` was empty, not earned.

Independent verification this shift:
- `tests/ai/smol/test_model_transport.py` is **429 lines**, single EFFORT-STOP NOTICE banner at 393-395, one copy of each notice test (`test_loop_limit_notice_for_agile_tier` 410, `..._for_max_tier` 420). The duplicated 354-383 block is gone.
- `qa_run_tests(suite="pytest", paths=["tests/ai/smol/test_model_transport.py"])` → **25 passed, 0 failed (12.1 s)**.

So: **the fix is real and the card is legitimately done.** Keeping it closed is correct.

The defect is in my gate, not in this card: `changed_files: 0` + `allow` is the same signature as the false green on `b618f7b4` (repo-root path rooted at `api/`) and on `e5841226` (35-of-1851 collection). This card passed by luck — someone ran the test suite directly afterwards. Had they not, `allow` on zero files would have shipped a shadowed-test deletion unverified.

No action needed here by the owner; the fix is tracked on `b618f7b4`.
